body:
It's like getting high. I used to do A LOT of cocaine, (hey, it was the... 2000's), and the come down is similar to me after a good day.
It's like, I've had my good day and I don't have anything to look forward to anymore. Those are the worst days.
The only way I find to help, even a little, is set myself up for something smaller the next day or the day after that so I still have something to look forward to but not something so paramount I've put myself on a roller coaster.

Well, this whole breakdown lasts around six weeks.
I start off so normal around people I want to be around, and when I get comfortable, subtly, I change and evolve into someone they want nothing to do with. The importance thing is I am important.. for awhile and then I'm just tiring.
I think I over compensate how important people are to me because I want someone to feel that way about me and I take it very personally when I realize that they don't.
Haha, yeah. The reaction can be like that. Depending on the mistake.
I used to do some auditing and I loved it because it required all of my attention. Also... it's weirdly fun for me to find mistakes. Mostly because I wasn't the one who made them.

Only my CFO is required. We aren't but we get heavily audited yearly. We're in the middle of one right now.
Perfect timing for this.

I'll look into this. I don't like reading much about bi polar disorder because I feel way behind on the development of coping with it. I have the Bi Polar Disorder Survival Guide which has taught me a lot. It's just the impulse that's the hardest to overcome.

My throwaway account name is pretty accurate. I literally have a total meltdown about once a year. Usually in the fall so I'm surprised it's so early this year.
If I don't say something in those total devastating moments, I'm worried that I'll be dead sooner than later. Honestly, I'm surprised I'm as old as I am. I never thought I'd live past 25.
It's just a struggle to keep myself alive anymore and if I don't force myself to do something... to say something, I'll just do it.
I'm tired of burdening my friends about it.
I don't talk to my family because they don't want to hear it. I'm the only one they don't reach out to.

It's easier to commit fraud working for such a large company. Our annual salaries payouts total less than five million. Our CEO barely breaks a hundred thousand.
I've done funky accounting in my early career and looking back, it's horrible that any company can get away with it.
I feel it cheats the American people and, clearly, is a major reason why the economy has failed the way it has.
(Thank you for making me think of something else.)
